clue.text: Banning tipping on jet

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so tipping comes after jet

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black, so the colour word stands for it
a ship tipping to one side is listing

explanation.surface: A ban on tipping the cabin crew aboard a jet airliner.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting someone on a list of the excluded is a way of barring or prohibiting them.

clue.text: Drunk as a snake?

definitions.meaning: slang for so intoxicated one cannot stand up
a snake literally has no limbs to walk on

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for very intoxicated, literally without the lower limbs, which a serpent also lacks.

clue.text: Is able to sign for Norwich City FC

parts.note: is able means can
Aries, the Ram, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A footballer able to put pen to paper and join Norwich City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' looks like signing a contract, but it is a zodiac sign. Norwich City is an English football club in East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow-shirted Norwich side's nickname refers to the songbirds, so the plural nickname stands for the club.

clue.text: Student, one with a tie

parts.note: L, the learner plate on a British car, stands for a student
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: A student who owns a single necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace a shoe or corset is to fasten it with cord, so the verb means tie.

clue.text: Singer has tension after her work

indicators.note: tension is placed after the words for her work

parts.note: a singer's work is a song
stress is mental tension

explanation.surface: A performer feels strain once her job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A songstress is a female vocalist, so a woman who sings fits.

clue.text: Nine get half ration — yet he got revolutionary punishment

parts.note: IX is nine in Roman numerals

indicators.note: half of the word ration is kept, here its closing three letters

explanation.surface: Nine people share half rations, while some man was punished by being spun round.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Ixion was bound to an ever-turning fiery wheel, hence 'revolutionary'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek king punished by Zeus on a spinning wheel is the mythical figure meant.

clue.text: Rejoiced in godlier fashion

indicators.note: in a new fashion means made into a different shape, so the letters of godlier are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone celebrated in a more pious way.
explanation.definitionFit: To glory in something is to delight or exult in it, a synonym of rejoiced.

clue.text: Keep it secret? Not at all!

definitions.meaning: a request not to speak of something
a polite reply to thanks, meaning it was no trouble

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase both asks for silence on a matter and politely brushes off gratitude.

clue.text: Coming back into office to check report

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
a statement is a report or account

explanation.surface: Returning to a job in order to check up on a report.
explanation.definitionFit: Restoring someone to a former post is the act of putting them back in office.

clue.text: Vital change in cargo

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of in and cargo

explanation.surface: An essential alteration to a ship's load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link, but it is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to living organisms or bodily organs, hence vital in the sense of fundamental to life.

clue.text: Offensive rumour about retired doctor

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rumour word goes around the other piece

parts.note: noise can mean talk or rumour, as in noises about a takeover

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the word for doctor goes backwards

parts.note: MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A nasty piece of gossip concerning a doctor who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like a doctor's career status, but it signals a backwards reading; 'about' places the turned doctor inside the rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome describes something foul-smelling or disgusting, a synonym of offensive.

clue.text: The one to the right of them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The person standing on the right-hand side of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessive determiner meaning belonging to those people.

clue.text: Capital city that could become an US icon

indicators.note: could become signals that the letters of an US icon may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A capital that might turn into an American symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunción is the capital of Paraguay.

clue.text: A colt needs schooling as a youngster

indicators.note: schooling means training or reshaping, so the letters of a colt needs are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young horse needs training while it is still young.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager between childhood and adulthood is a youngster.

clue.text: Long-running TV programme possibly needs a rest

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of needs a rest might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A show that has run for decades perhaps deserves a break.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap opera set in east London, running since 1985.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC soap has been on air since 1985, so it is a long-running television show.

clue.text: Press boss has no alternative but to revise

indicators.note: has no means the alternative word is taken away

parts.note: the boss of a newspaper is its editor
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A newspaper chief has no choice but to rewrite the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit text is to correct or revise it.

clue.text: Its promoters will raise no obstacles of course

definitions.text: Its promoters will raise no obstacles of course

parts.words: Its promoters will raise no obstacles of course
parts.note: a race run over a racecourse with no fences or hurdles, so organisers set up no jumps on the course

explanation.surface: Organisers who naturally will not stand in anyone's way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but means on the racecourse; obstacles are jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race without jumps is run on level turf, and its organisers put no hurdles on the track.

clue.text: Precisely where a driver is heading, say

indicators.note: say means the words are spoken, so we write what they sound like

parts.note: a golfer's driver is used from a tee, so it heads to a tee

explanation.surface: Exactly where a motorist is going, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' looks like a motorist, but it is a golf club, used to strike off a tee.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom meaning exactly or perfectly, as in fits to a T.

clue.text: Increase gun team in action

indicators.note: in action means put to work and moving about, so the letters of gun team are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reinforce the artillery crew while they are firing.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment something is to enlarge or add to it, so it means increase.

clue.text: Torch provides illumination for a photographer

definitions.meaning: a camera flash is light for taking pictures

explanation.definitionFit: The American word for a portable electric lamp, and literally the burst of light from a camera.

clue.text: Attempt to pocket a ball, but lose one's nerve

parts.note: a go is an attempt
in snooker, to pot is to sink a ball into a pocket

explanation.surface: A snooker player tries a shot but then bottles it.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a cue game, popular in Britain; 'to' is kept as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to fall apart or deteriorate, as someone whose composure fails.

clue.text: Player given an awful roasting

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of roasting are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A sportsman gets a terrible telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roasting' looks like a fierce criticism of a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the organ is a musical player.

clue.text: Cultivating a vine is simple

indicators.note: cultivating means working the ground, so the letters of a vine are turned over

explanation.surface: Growing grapes is easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means unsophisticated or artless, which is a sense of simple.

clue.text: Image to carry on the first of March

parts.note: to tote is to carry

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A picture to be carried at the start of March.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a carved emblem or symbol, a kind of image.

clue.text: Tax man north of the Tweed

definitions.meaning: an old word for a levy
a man from Scotland, the River Tweed forming part of the border with England

explanation.definitionFit: An archaic payment surviving in 'scot-free', and a native of Scotland.

clue.text: I seem somehow to follow it in detail

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the word it
somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters of I seem are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone seems to understand it thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to list item by item, which is to detail.

clue.text: The climber's sole aid

parts.note: a spiked frame strapped to the sole of a boot helps a climber on ice

explanation.surface: The only help a mountaineer has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' reads as 'only', but it is the underside of the boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiked metal plate fixed under a boot to grip ice, literally an aid attached to the sole.

clue.text: High in visual acuity scores

parts.note: a score is twenty, and the plural gives two of them
a score is twenty, and the plural gives two of them

explanation.surface: Marks for sharp eyesight that come out top.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye-test rating for normal sharp sight, measured on a Snellen chart.
